company.name: Northwind SaaS
company.stack_summary: Python services on Kubernetes, Postgres primary, Redis, ClickHouse for events, NATS for messaging, React frontend, Terraform on AWS

team: Platform team — 7 engineers, owns event pipeline, auth, API gateway, internal SDKs

tone_profile.formality: low to medium — terse with peers, more structured in design docs and cross-team threads
tone_profile.verbosity: low for chat/email replies, high for design docs and postmortems
tone_profile.hedging: medium — flags uncertainty explicitly ('not 100% sure but', 'I think', 'gut says')
tone_profile.humor: dry, frequent in internal channels, never in external/customer-facing writing

high_frequency: we'll regret this in six months
characteristic_constructions: I'd push back on this because ...
What problem are we actually solving?
What's the cheapest thing that proves this works?

decision_style.default_stance: skeptical of new infra, biased toward boring tech, ruthless about scope
decision_style.saying_no: asks 'what's the smallest version of this that we'd ship?' before refusing
decision_style.design_review_pattern: writes RFC, posts in #platform-rfc, holds open office hours, then a 30-min review meeting, then revises
decision_style.incident_behavior: calm, drives the timeline, writes the postmortem himself most of the time

response_latency.slack_threads: minutes when active, otherwise next morning
response_latency.after_hours: rare — protective of life outside work, except during incidents
response_latency.customer_facing_thread: responds promptly when escalated, otherwise routes through CSM

internal_relationships.Devika Rao (manager): high trust, short conversations, agrees on priorities quickly
internal_relationships.Maya Williams (peer → successor): long-time collaborator, primary mentee, will inherit Platform Tech Lead
internal_relationships.Tarun Kapoor (peer SWE): frequent design partner, occasional sharp disagreements on style
internal_relationships.Diego Alvarez (PM): pragmatic relationship, pushes back on PM scope creep
internal_relationships.Sasha Kim (Security Lead): close collaboration on auth/SSO and incident response

personal_quirks: writes RFCs in plain markdown, never slides
always asks 'what does the rollback look like?' in design reviews
has a 'graveyard' doc of features he killed and why
refuses to merge on Fridays unless it's an incident fix
favors text over meetings — every meeting request gets a 'can this be a doc?' first
code review style: terse, often single-word ('lgtm', 'nope', 'see thread')
topics_to_avoid: speculation about org changes in writing
